A report's code lists, with the ones its layers give

Source: R/spec_ard.R
tfl_report_codelists.Rd

tfl_report_codelists() gives the code lists the ARD program of each report is written with. A report's code lists can come from the layers it extends – the study's defaults.yml, a pattern – as well as from its own file (tfl_resolve_output() puts them together for the RTF); the sheets (tfl_sheets_from_yaml()) hold a report's own only, so that they stay the round trip back to the YAML. This is the sheets' codelists rows with the layers' lists added, report by report.

Usage

tfl_report_codelists(study, outputs = NULL, rows = NULL)

Arguments

study

The study's spec, as tfl_read_study_spec() reads it.

outputs

The reports, as tfl_sheets_from_spec() takes them: a list of tfl_output named by id. NULL (default): the study's own files, read as tfl_sheets_from_yaml() reads them.

rows

The reports' own code list rows (the sheets' codelists, a template's lists among them), when the caller has them: the sheets are then not made again. The result keeps the columns of rows (a layer's rows have NA there), and a row of a report not in outputs stays. NULL (default): made from outputs.

Value

A data frame of the sheets' codelists rows (output_id, variable, value, label, order, under), the reports in the TOC's order; every row has its report (no NA output_id), and zero rows when no report has a list. tfl_ard_code() and tfl_build_ard() write a study's ARD with these.

Details

For each report and variable there is one list: the report's own when it has one (a template's own lists among them, as the sheets hold them), else the one of the layers it extends (a pattern's over the defaults'). A report that extends nothing (extends: none) has only its own.

Examples

d <- system.file("extdata", "spec-yaml", package = "tflspec")
tfl_report_codelists(tfl_read_study_spec(d))
#>   output_id variable   value          label order under
#> 1  T-14-1-1   TRT01A  Drug X  Drug X 200 mg     1  <NA>
#> 2  T-14-1-1   TRT01A Control Control 100 mg     2  <NA>
